issues.explanation: At 12:00 today the ferry was not moored at the far bank, so by the supplied rule the crossing cannot have been complete at that same time.

evidence.excerpt: A ferry crossing is complete only when the ferry is moored at the far bank.
At 12:00 today the ferry was still mid-river and not moored at the far bank.

issues.reasoning: F2 places the same ferry still mid-river and not moored at the far bank at 12:00 today, the same literal time stated in the claim, so object and time scope coincide; F1 supplies the static-canon rule that a crossing is complete only when the ferry is moored at the far bank, which governs the claim's completion outcome. Jointly they make 'complete at 12:00 today' impossible at that moment; no later transition is offered. F1 is a premise (context), F2 the direct contradicting fact.

suggested_revision.before: At 12:00 today the ferry crossing was complete.
suggested_revision.after: At 12:00 today the ferry crossing was not yet complete.
